entry.title: WIP: perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): reduce compile time (#570)
entry.content:
<pre style='white-space:pre-wrap;width:81ex'>WIP: perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): reduce compile time (#570)
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): record instance-resolution results as shortcuts
Typeclass inference was about 37% of the project's CPU time. On the concrete function spaces of the Euler half (L² spaces, the cylinder Sobolev space, closed subspaces of them) each derived structure such as `AddCommMonoid`, `Module ℝ` or `TopologicalSpace` was rediscovered by a search through failing subobject branches, once per declaration.
Add `ForMathlib/NormedSpaceShortcuts` with three commands that record, for a carrier `X`, the instances resolution currently finds and register them as instances of `X`. All recorded instances are elaborated before any is registered, so terms elaborated with and without the shortcuts agree up to unfolding the shortcut.
Use them for `Lp E 2 μ`, `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` and its Lebesgue measure, the cylinder Sobolev space, the solenoidal, homogeneous, supported and matching subspaces, and the two space-time products.
Full project build on 16 cores: 12,146 s -> 8,621 s user CPU for the 1,325 rebuilt modules plus dependents, 16:37 -> 12:02 wall. No statement or proof changes.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): operator-space shortcuts and cheaper map coercions
- The shortcut for `SeminormedAddCommGroup X` is now the seminormed group underlying the recorded `NormedAddCommGroup X`, so a `NormedSpace ℝ X` request coming from `[NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]` matches the recorded instance without comparing two seminormed structures. - Record the normed-space instances of the continuous linear maps between two Euclidean spaces, two `L²` spaces, and the cylinder Sobolev and lifted `L²` spaces. - `ForMathlib/LinearMapShortcuts`: high-priority copies of the function coercion and additive homomorphism classes of continuous linear maps and linear isometries, answered from the shape of the map type. - `initialDatum_support`: rewrite with new `packets_one`, `stages_one` and `Stage.successor_zero`/`successor_succ` equations instead of unifying two packet stages field by field (17 s -> 0.1 s).
Full project build on 16 cores, modules downstream of a change (1,335): summed per-module time 11,232 s -> 8,209 s against the baseline, wall 16:37 -> 10:43.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): make the slowest declarations cheap to check
About sixty declarations spent 0.5-20 s each in unification or kernel conversion although their proofs are one or two lines. The common cause is an `exact`, `change` or term-mode proof whose two sides agree only after unfolding a large definition under a structure projection, a coercion or an arithmetic operation; Lean then unfolds both sides and compares them field by field. The proofs now make the two sides syntactically equal first:
- rewrite with a closed `rfl` equation between two applications (`packets_one`, `Stage.forwardNext_state`, `Stage.joinedState_eq`, `GeometryJoinedChoice.state_velocity`, `Parent.extendPath_field`, ...), - unfold the relevant abbreviations with `dsimp only`/`rw` before `exact`, - pass implicit type arguments of bundled operators explicitly so their coercion is resolved with known types, - replace `nlinarith`, `convert!` and `simp` with a commutativity lemma in the simp set by the explicit steps they found.
No statement changes. The three `MemLp W 2` hypotheses of `R3/PressureFunctionals` now name the measure, which is the term the default argument already produced.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): drop Sobolev operator shortcuts, name operator type arguments
- Remove the shortcut batteries for the three operator spaces between the cylinder Sobolev and lifted L² spaces. An interleaved benchmark showed they save about 2.5% on the files using those spaces but cost 9 s where they are declared, a wash for the project. - `ForMathlib/BoundedContinuousFunctionShortcuts`: derive `ContinuousAdd (α →ᵇ β)` from the additive group first. For values in a normed ring it was found through the ring, whose addition the kernel then had to compare with the group addition in every declaration mentioning continuous linear maps out of `C(K, α →ᵇ β)`. - Name the value space of `translate` and `average` in six statements of the `CylinderDirichlet*` files. The bundled operator was applied before its type argument was known, which makes instance resolution re-check the whole coercion instance. Elaborated types are unchanged (compared by hash for all 59k declarations); the three files go from 23.5 s to 17.1 s.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): second pass over slow declarations
A second sweep over the declarations that a fresh per-declaration profile ranks slowest (about 190 declarations in 70 files). The recurring causes and fixes:
* Bundled operators applied before their type arguments are known (`pathTranslate P a u`, `fullMultiplierMap P A u`, `A.adjoint v`): the function coercion is resolved with metavariables in the instance problem. The implicit type arguments are now named in the statement and proof text. The elaborated statements are unchanged; for 42 of them the arguments of a universe-level `max` are listed in a different order. * `exact` / `change` across definitions whose bodies differ only in instance paths or proof terms: unfold the local definition and compare with `with_reducible`, or rewrite with a closed `rfl` equation first. * `let` before a hypothesis is stated: replaced by `set` after it, so the hypothesis and the goal agree syntactically. * `nlinarith` / `linarith` on goals that are linear in a few products: explicit monotonicity lemmas and `linarith only`. * `rw` chains on large goals (each step type-checks a motive): one `simp only`. * Associativity-commutativity `simp` sets: `ring` or one explicit rewrite. * Measurability side goals that searched for second countability of the codomain, and `toLp` applications with an unassigned measure.
41 lemmas are added (equation lemmas for definitions that were unfolded by unification, three generic helpers); no declaration is removed and no statement is changed. Two definitions change in proof arguments only.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): name the type arguments of applied operators
The bundled operators of the Euler half (`pathTranslate`, `includePath`, `fullOperatorMap`, `supportedMultiplierMap`, `ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint`, `rankOne`, ...) take their carrier types as implicit arguments that only the result type mentions. At an application such as `pathTranslate P a u` Lean has to coerce the bundled map to a function before it knows these types, so the `CoeFun` instance problem is solved with metavariables in every structure of the map type. A heartbeat trace shows this single kind of query costing between 30 ms and 0.5 s per application and about 5% of all elaboration work of the project, concentrated in a quarter of the files.
This commit names the implicit arguments at the applications (`pathTranslate (K := K) (V := V) P a u`, `adjoint (𝕜 := ℝ) (E := U) (F := V) A v`) in 192 files: 692 statements and the corresponding lines inside proofs and definition bodies. No proof is restructured.
The elaborated terms are unchanged: comparing every declaration of the project before and after, no statement and no definition value differs (93 statements list the arguments of a universe-level `max` in another order). Where naming an argument made Lean select a different instance, the application is left as it was.
Measured by the deterministic heartbeat count of each file (single-threaded, imports excluded), the edited files need 22% less work in total, between 3% and 78% per file.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): name operator arguments in section hypotheses
A second, deterministic scan (heartbeat trace of 516 files) listed the instance problems that are still solved with unknown types after the previous commit. Most of them come from three places, fixed here in 183 files:
* Hypotheses on `variable` lines, such as `(hp : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun a => pathTranslate P a p))`. A section hypothesis is elaborated again by every declaration of its section, so one unnamed application cost 300 to 5000 units in each of them. The applications now name their type arguments. * Applications in statements, proofs and definition bodies that the first pass missed, including `rankOne`, `multilinearBundling`, `pathEvaluation`, `weight`/`normalize` and lemma applications whose implicit types were only fixed by a later argument. * Overloaded names whose wrong candidate was tried first and failed on an expensive coercion (`chartEquiv`, `extend`, `Budget`, `univ`): the intended one is selected by a named argument or the qualified name.
As before the elaborated terms are unchanged: no statement and no definition value differs across the 59,786 declarations of the project, private ones included (26 statements list the arguments of a universe-level `max` in another order). Applications where every spelling made Lean select a different instance are left as they were.
Heartbeat count of the edited files: 14% to 67% less work in the files with section hypotheses, 1.6 million units (about 15%) less over all edited files.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): resolve unknown types before unification
A project-wide heartbeat scan listed, per declaration, the instance problems that still contain metavariables and the unifications with metavariables that fail. 179 files are edited; the causes and the edits are:
* Failed expected-type propagation. A lemma is applied to a term whose implicit types or functions are not yet known (`HasDerivAt.comp`, `comp_hasDerivAt` with a `prodMk` argument, `integral_integral_swap`, `opNorm_comp_le` on an unapplied operator); Lean tries to unify the expected type first, fails after 400 to 7000 units and retries. The implicit type or function is now named at the application (`comp_hasDerivAt (F := ℝ × ℝ)`, `(f := fun s => (s, x))`). * Overloaded names. With two open namespaces defining `Field`, `Inner`, `inner`, `range`, `average`, `profile`, `slope`, `extend` or `integral`, every use elaborated the wrong candidate first and failed on a coercion. The intended declaration is written with its qualified name (about 700 occurrences). * A cheap instance problem repeated hundreds of times because one operator or lemma had an unknown type argument; one named argument removes all of them. * Undetermined numerals and measures inside proofs: `^ 2` in the first step of a `calc` and the defaulted measure of `SchwartzMap.memLp` are unknown while the step is unified, so the unification fails and is retried. They are written `^ (2 : ℕ)` and `volume`.
No statement and no definition value differs across the 59,786 declarations (9 statements list the arguments of a universe-level `max` in another order). Heartbeat count of the edited files: 1.5 million units less, 13% of their work.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): shortcut instances for coercions and for ℝ
Two kinds of instance problem occur in nearly every declaration, are answered by a search through general instances each time, and are not shared between declarations:
* coercions: a set or subobject used as a type, an element of a subtype used in the ambient type, `∞` as a smoothness order. The chain of coercion classes tries the other kinds of coercion first (about 40 heartbeat units per query, 780 to 2300 for elements of a submodule of a function space); * facts about `ℝ`: characteristic zero, monotonicity of addition and multiplication, continuity of the operations (20 to 120 units each), derived from the ordered or normed field structure after unrelated attempts.
`ForMathlib/ElaborationShortcuts.lean` registers the coercion instances that resolution already finds, with high priority, and states the facts about `ℝ` as instances. It is imported by the 79 files from which every other file of the project reaches it through public imports; the 24 files whose imports do not include normed spaces are left without it.
The coercion shortcuts unfold to the same coercion, and the facts about `ℝ` are propositions, so no structure that resolution finds changes. Compared with the previous commit, 3,839 statements and 413 definition values carry a different proof term in an instance argument; after erasing proof terms every statement and every definition value of the project is identical.
Interleaved benchmark on 200 random files against `main`: -27.0% before this commit, -27.8% with it. This commit rebuilds 1,569 of the 1,593 modules: 8,565 s user CPU and 12:00 wall, against 12,146 s and 16:37 for the full build of `main` on the same machine.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): avoid two expensive closing attempts
`congr 1` in `next_oscillation_periodic` and `next_pressure_periodic` first tried to close the goal by `rfl`, unfolding both sums (half of the work of `CycleMeanEquation`); the congruence is now given as a term. A `simpa` in `sourceJets_sub_bound` that only needed `one_mul` searched the norm instances of the axis space; it is replaced by the term.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): the 490 most expensive declarations
A deterministic per-declaration scan (heartbeat counts of every command of the project) ranked the declarations by elaboration work; the 487 declarations above 11,000 units (about a second each) were 14% of the total. In 201 files their proofs now avoid the expensive step the trace pointed to:
* generic `map_zero`/`map_add`/`map_smul` rewrites and `rw` chains on large goals: specific lemmas, `simp only`, or a `congrArg`/`Eq.trans` term; * `nlinarith`, `gcongr` and `positivity` on goals that are linear in a few products or monotone in explicit factors: the monotonicity lemma and `linarith only`; `linarith` over a large context: `linarith only`; * `ext <;> simp`, `fin_cases <;> simp`, `field_simp` and associativity- commutativity `simp` sets: `simp only` with the lemmas used, `ring`, `linear_combination`; * `exact`, `change` and `convert` across definitions that agree only after unfolding: `rfl` equation lemmas, `with_reducible exact`, `congr_deriv`; * repeated failing searches (`SecondCountableTopologyEither` on the codomain, a closure search over `ContDiffAt` and `AnalyticAt`): the instance or the closure lemma given directly.
28 lemmas are added, among them general ones such as `bound_add`/`bound_mul` for monotone envelopes, `sum_mul_smul_left`, `linearIsometryEquiv_integral_comm` and `const_smul_majorant_bound`. A local notation used once is written out, and three local notations are parenthesized so that no unexpander is generated for them. No statement and no definition value changes.
Heartbeat count of the edited files: about 2 million units less, 10% to 90% per file.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): second pass over the most expensive declarations
Rework the proofs of the declarations that still cost at least 8,000 thousand heartbeats each (491 declarations in 314 files were examined; 242 files changed). No statement changes: every declaration type is identical, and definition values differ at most inside proof terms.
The fixes, by frequency: - `rw` chains and `change` on large goals replaced by one `simp only` or by `congrArg`/`Eq.trans` terms (avoids repeated motive checks and unfolding during unification); - `nlinarith`, `linarith`, `positivity`, `gcongr` and `field_simp` replaced by explicit lemma applications or `linarith only [...]`; - specific `ContinuousLinearMap.map_*` lemmas instead of generic `map_*`, and `apply` instead of `exact` where the conclusion was unified twice; - right-hand sides of long `local notation`s parenthesized, so that no unexpander is generated for them; - local `SecondCountableTopologyEither` facts in front of `aestronglyMeasurable` goals on multilinear-map-valued functions.
New helper lemmas: 25 (equation lemmas and small general facts).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): `linarith only` with the hypotheses each call uses
Rewrite 4,459 bare `linarith` / `nlinarith` calls in 360 files as `linarith only [...]`, listing the local hypotheses that the finished proof of each call uses (read off its proof term), followed by the call's own extra terms. Without `only`, linarith preprocesses every hypothesis in scope, and in these proofs the contexts are large.
Calls were converted only where every run of the call (for example under `<;>`) used named, unshadowed hypotheses and its goal had no metavariables; each changed file was recompiled, and kept only if its elaboration got at least 0.3% cheaper (saving 645k thousand heartbeats in total).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): `simp only` with the lemmas `simp?` reports
Replace about 3,400 bare `simp`, `simpa` and `dsimp` calls in 287 files by the `simp only [...]` (`simpa only`, `dsimp only`) form that `simp?` / `dsimp?` suggests for them. A bare `simp` searches the whole default simp set at every subterm, and Mathlib's `linter.flexible` tracks what every bare `simp` touches; both costs go away.
Each changed file was recompiled; calls whose suggestion did not compile were left as they were, and a file was kept only if its elaboration got at least 0.3% cheaper (saving 367k thousand heartbeats in total).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): parenthesize long local notations
For a variable-free `local notation "X" => f a b c`, Lean generates an unexpander whose pattern is the whole right-hand side, and compiling it costs up to a second per notation. With the right-hand side in parentheses no unexpander is generated; the notation elaborates as before, but goals display the expanded term instead of `X`. Applied to the 27 files where it helps (saving 100k thousand heartbeats).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): third pass, the Navier–Stokes half
Rework the proofs of the 330 Navier–Stokes declarations that cost at least 5,000 thousand heartbeats and had not been examined before (130 files changed). These long real-analysis estimates spend most of their time in Mathlib tactics running in the interpreter:
- `nlinarith`, `positivity` and `gcongr` replaced by explicit lemma applications (`one_le_mul_of_one_le_of_one_le`, `pow_le_pow_left₀`, `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left`, …), `linarith` over fixed coefficients by `linear_combination`; - `field_simp` by `div_mul_cancel₀`-style rewrites or `linear_combination e * mul_inv_cancel₀ h`, `ring_nf` by `ring` (it was failing a `CharZero` search on function types); - `fin_cases <;> simp` and `ext <;> simp` by vector-level `simp only`; - failed expected-type propagation avoided by naming the function in `HasFDerivAt.comp` / `HasDerivAt.scomp`, or by `(e :)`; - local `SecondCountableTopologyEither` facts for parametric integrals.
No statement changes. 16 lemmas are added (rfl equation lemmas and small general facts such as `pack_congr`, `comp_vecCons6`, `SameCarrier.trans`).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): fourth pass, the Euler half
Rework the proofs of the 420 most expensive Euler declarations that no earlier pass had examined (6,300–10,700 thousand heartbeats each; 187 files changed). Besides the causes handled before (`rw` chains and `change` on large goals, generic `map_*` lemmas, typed `have`s that restate instance-heavy types, `positivity`/`gcongr`/`nlinarith`):
- the bare name `normalize` is ambiguous with Mathlib's `_root_.normalize` where `EulerContinuousTimeWeight` is open; every use first failed on the Mathlib name. Uses in the edited files are now qualified; - in a few long statements the numeric exponents carry a `(k : ℕ)` ascription: each bare literal exponent leaves a default-instance problem that is retried after every binder; - `h.continuousLinearMap_comp L` instead of `L.contDiff.comp h`, local `SecondCountableTopologyEither` facts, and failing `rfl` branches of `first | rfl | …` removed.
No statement changes. 9 lemmas are added.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): numeric exponents as natural numbers at once
A numeric exponent such as the `2` in `x ^ 2` is elaborated with an unknown type that only the default instance fixes, at the end. In a statement every such pending problem is retried after each later binder, so long estimates with many powers cost quadratically: one statement of `PacketNeighborControlled` took 9,121 thousand heartbeats, 1,129 with the exponents ascribed.
In the 84 files where it measurably helps (at least 1% and 300 thousand heartbeats; 242k in total), a one-line local rule makes Lean read a numeral exponent as `(n : ℕ)` directly:
local macro_rules | `($x ^ $n:num) => `($x ^ ($n : ℕ))
The elaborated terms are the ones the default instance chose before: no statement or definition value changes. Elsewhere the rule is neutral or slightly slower, so it is not made global.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* perf(NavierStokesAndEuler): qualify `EulerContinuousTimeWeight.normalize`
Where `EulerContinuousTimeWeight` is open, the bare name `normalize` also denotes Mathlib's `_root_.normalize`; every use elaborated the Mathlib candidate first and failed on a `NormalizationMonoid` search and a coercion of its argument (300–400 thousand heartbeats each, repeated for `variable` hypotheses in every declaration). The 74 remaining uses in 15 files now use the qualified name. No statement changes.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
* style(NavierStokesAndEuler): prove `∞ ≠ 0` by a term
The squeezed `simp only [ne_eq, WithTop.coe_eq_zero, ENat.top_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true]` that closed the side condition of `ContDiffAt.differentiableAt` and its relatives (the smoothness order `∞` is nonzero) is replaced by the direct term `WithTop.coe_ne_zero.2 ENat.top_ne_zero`: shorter than both that list and the original `by simp`, and without a `simp` call. 319 occurrences in 75 files; no statement changes.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
